Question 1
?

Calculate dydx for y=−4+2x7−12x2+x5/4.

a
14x6−24x+5x44
b
14x6+22x−5x144
c
14x6+24x+5x−144
d
2x6−24x+54x3
e
14x6−12x2+5x124
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

dydx=ddx(−4+2x7−12x2+x5/4)=ddx(−4)+ddx(2x7)−ddx(12x2)+ddx(x5/4)=ddx(−4)+2⋅ddx(x7)−12⋅ddx(x2)+ddx(x5/4)=0+2⋅7x(7−1)−12⋅2x(2−1)+54⋅x(54−1)=14x6−24x+54x1/4=14x6−24x+5x44

q-10292.worked_solution:
Here, we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{7}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}+2x-2) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{7})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{7})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-2})+2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2) \\  & =2\cdot 7{x}^{(7-1)}+(-2){x}^{(-2-1)}+2\cdot 1-0 \\  & =14{x}^{6}-2{x}^{-3}+2 \\  & =14{x}^{6}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}+2\end{aligned}
$$

q-10292.html:
Question 2
?

Calculate dydx for y=2x7+1x2+2x−2.

a
7x6−2x3+2
b
14x6−2x3+2
c
14x6−2x3−2
d
14x6−2x3
e
14x6+2x3+2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

dydx=ddx(2x7+1x2+2x−2)=ddx(2x7)+ddx(x−2)+ddx(2x)−ddx(2)=2⋅ddx(x7)+ddx(x−2)+2⋅ddx(x)−ddx(2)=2⋅7x(7−1)+(−2)x(−2−1)+2⋅1−0=14x6−2x−3+2=14x6−2x3+2

q-70507.name: Question 3
q-70507.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is the sum of three power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{8}-{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{8})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-2}) \\  & =8{x}^{(8-1)}-3{x}^{(3-1)}+(-2){x}^{-2-1} \\  & =8{x}^{7}-3{x}^{2}-2{x}^{-3} \\  & =8{x}^{7}-3{x}^{2}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-70510.name: Question 4
q-70510.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is the sum of three power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+\sqrt{x}-\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{1/2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-1}) \\  & =2{x}^{(2-1)}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{1/2-1}-(-1){x}^{(-1-1)} \\  & =2x+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}+{x}^{-2} \\  & =2x+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We first rewrite the function as

$$
y=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}=\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3/2}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-3/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-\frac{3}{2}){x}^{(-\frac{3}{2}-1)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-5/2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}\end{aligned}

If y=13x3, find dydx.

a

b
1x3
c
−12x5
d
−13x
e
12x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We first rewrite the function as y=13x3=13x−3/2.

Then, we apply the constant multiple and power rules:

dydx=ddx(13x−3/2)=13⋅ddx(x−3/2)=13⋅(−32)x(−32−1)=−12x−5/2=−12x5
